question_text: Estimate the length of dendrites in the freezing of copper alloys containing, (a) $5 \% \mathrm{Zn}$, (b) $5 \% \mathrm{Sn}$, and (c) $0.05 \% \mathrm{Sn}$. In each case, assume a thermal gradient of $G=0.5^{\circ} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{mm}$ and assume the temperatures at the tips and bases of the dendrites are the equilibrium for liquidus and solidus temperatures the alloy. Assume the freezing ranges for the alloys are: (a) $5 \% \mathrm{Zn}, 6^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$; (b) $5 \% \mathrm{Sn}, 130^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$; and (c) $0.05 \% \mathrm{Sn}, 1.3^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Give your answer as a tuple: (dendrite_length_5pct_Zn, dendrite_length_5pct_Sn, dendrite_length_0.05pct_Sn).The units of each required answer are (mm, mm, mm), respectively.
response:
The calculations are confirmed. The dendrite length scales directly with the freezing range — the larger the freezing range, the longer the dendrites must be to span the temperature interval at the given gradient.
